$comment: The ONE source for the docs' package catalogue (hub docs/19, gate R7). Every feature, deprecation, retirement or version bump updates this file in the same change. Fields: id (card anchor #pkg-<id>), kind (package | design | feature: a retired or shelved part of the framework that never had its own npm name), npm (null when there is no npm name), repo (GitHub URL, null until the repo exists), category, summary (one line), status (available | preview | in-development | planned | shelved | retired), phase (roadmap phase, blueprint 18 §10; null when it doesn't apply), since (the docs line in which this status started, or null), replacement (required for retired), docs (a page slug of this docs version, or null), checklist (number in the hub's 47-package master list, docs/research/2026-11-14-package-checklist.md), note (optional). Phases 1-3 follow blueprint §10 (agent-tools and social-login moved up to phase 2); phases 4-8 follow the master list.

packages.summary: The framework: container, config, routing, controllers, validation, ORM, migrations, logging, authorization, tenancy and the node strut command line.
Sign-in, registration, password reset, email verification, 2FA, passkeys, API tokens, teams and impersonation.
The React admin's behaviour: auto CRUD screens, tables, forms, sidebar, command palette. The look comes from a design package.
The installer behind npm create strutvane@latest: questions, then a migrated, seeded app.
The small npx strutvane command: the same as node strut inside a project, a pointer to create one outside.
packages.note: Which repository holds it is still open.

packages.summary: The logs screen at /_strutvane/logs: live tail, search and download. Logging itself is in the framework.
packages.note: The repository is still named strutvane-logs; it is renamed to strutvane-log-viewer (ADR-0022).

packages.summary: The default design: clean, minimal, quiet colours, dense readable tables.
packages.note: Default in the installer. The look is proven as a mockup (spike 19).

packages.summary: A colourful design with soft-shadow cards, gradient charts and roomier spacing.
packages.note: The look is proven as a mockup (spike 17).

packages.summary: Redis and Valkey drivers for cache, queue, locks, sessions, rate limits and broadcasting.
Jobs, failures, retries and scheduled tasks on one screen.
S3 and Azure disks, presigned and resumable uploads, virus scanning and quotas.
Meilisearch and Typesense engines, and hybrid vector search.
CSV and XLSX import with column mapping and a dry run; policy-aware exports.
A development recorder for requests, queries, jobs, mail and policy decisions.
OpenTelemetry export and a self-hosted metrics dashboard.
Scheduled health checks, history, alerts and an uptime endpoint.
AGENTS.md, skills, a local docs MCP server and offline docs search for AI coding assistants.
packages.note: Moved up to phase 2 (blueprint §10); the master list still says 3.

packages.summary: Chart and KPI widgets suggested from your tables, fed by a policy- and tenant-safe aggregate endpoint.
Dashboard pages, per-user layouts, filters and scheduled digests.
Per-record change history, an activity feed and an audit explorer.
Typed, database-backed app, team and user settings with generated pages.
Attachments, image conversions, responsive images and a media manager.
Team-scoped, typed tags on any model.
Threaded comments, mentions and reactions on any record.
PDFs such as invoices and reports from React templates.
GDPR data export and erasure, consent and retention.
Encrypted database and storage backups, with restore drills.
An interactive OpenAPI explorer with try-it-out.
Sign in with Google, Microsoft, GitHub and Apple.
packages.note: Moved up to phase 2 (blueprint §10); the master list still says 5.

packages.summary: Per-team OIDC and SAML single sign-on, SCIM and domain verification.
An OAuth 2.1 provider, so other apps can sign in with yours.
Lets AI agents use your app through MCP, under your policies and teams.
Typed feature flags per user, team or plan.
Signed outgoing webhooks with retries, and verification of incoming ones.
A GraphQL API generated from your models, policies and teams.
SaaS subscriptions, seats and entitlements per team.
Numbered invoices with tax, credit notes and PDFs.
A WebSocket server, channels and live tables.
SMS, Slack, Teams, web push and WhatsApp next to email, with a preference centre.
Kanban board and calendar views over any resource.
Editable, per-team transactional mail templates.
AI model calls, structured output, embeddings and policy-bound agent tools.
Durable workflows, approvals, timers and state machines.
Database-backed UI strings and translatable record fields.
Forms designed by admins, and custom fields per team.
Pages, blocks, menus, redirects, SEO and a sitemap.
Playwright fixtures for testing the real UI in a browser.
One-off payments from your own customers through a hosted checkout.
Spatial columns, distance queries, geocoding and map views.
A translucent "glass" design direction, explored as a mockup (spike 18).
packages.note: Shelved on 2026-11-15 in favour of Crisp and Vivid. It is the first candidate for a future design package.

packages.summary: v1's upgrade command and its three-way merge of generated files.

packages.summary: Better Auth as v1's default identity engine.
packages.replacement: @strutvane/auth's own engine, with its tables as ordinary migrations in your app
